ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: The visible ventral surface displays a ratio of approximately 65% high-intensity (white/off-white) pixels to 35% low-intensity (black/dark-grey) pixels.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Low-intensity pixels are concentrated in a contiguous region surrounding the median notch and extending along the proximal trailing edge. The high-intensity lateral lobes are populated with numerous isolated, low-intensity geometric clusters (mottling) of varying sizes, with a higher density of small spots on the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, acute V-shaped depression with a calculated internal angle of approximately 50 degrees and a significant vertical depth relative to the fluke horizontal axis.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration profile along the entire trailing edge boundary, characterized by sharp peaks and narrow valleys with a variation amplitude of approximately 2-5 pixels.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex curvature across the trailing edge of both lobes, tapering into sharp, slightly elevated distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Widespread detection of circular and oval high-contrast dark pixel clusters (3-12 pixels in diameter) localized on the high-intensity fields, consistent with barnacle-related scarring patterns.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Heavy, irregular pixel buildup and ragged fragmentation at the extreme distal tips of both lobes, indicating significant colonization by sessile organisms or associated mechanical wear.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced asymmetric pigmentation boundary where the dark central region extends significantly further toward the mid-point of the right lobe trailing edge compared to the left.
